text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Police who refused to body search Kurdish rebel suicide bomber because she was a woman paid with their lives when she set off the bomb in their car. Six people died in the explosion in the central town of Sivas.
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz slams Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan for trying to persuade his Motherland Party MPs to join the government.
- Police averted a second suicide bomb attack in the southeastern city of Diyarbakir. Would-be bomber was arrested.
- Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller denies she will wait for corruption charges against her to be lifted and then break the coalition with Erbakan.
- The people celebrate Republic Day despite terrorism and rise of Islamist extremism.
- Istanbul to host meeting of British tourism association.
- Islamist wing of coalition admits it needs the IMF to secure foreign credit.
- Labour unions preparing for collective bargaining talks on November 1, three months earlier than usual.
